## Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


10/21/2026


Download (opens in new window)


WILMINGTON, N.C., Oct. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Live Oak Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: LOB) (“Live Oak” or “the Company”) today reported third quarter of 2026 net income attributable to common shareholders of $24.3 million, or $0.52 per diluted common share.


Live Oak’s performance in the quarter, compared to the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, includes these notable items:


- Net interest income increased 6.1% and 15.2% compared to the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively. Net interest margin decreased 3 basis points during the third quarter of 2026 from 3.33% for the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025 to 3.30%
- Revenue (comprised of net interest income and noninterest income) increased 12.5% and 23.4% compared to the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively, and noninterest expense increased 1.4% and 2.6% compared to the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively, which generated a 25.6% and 52.9% increase in pre-provision net revenue1 compared to the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively
- Strong loan production of $2.1 billion accompanied by strong deposit growth of $920.6 million during the third quarter of 2026, compared to June 30, 2026, with total assets growing by 5.8% and 15.7% to $17.0 billion as of September 30, 2026, compared to June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025, respectively
- Provision expense for credit losses of $54.7 million for the third quarter of 2026, increased $28.9 million and $32.5 million compared to the second quarter of 2026 and third quarter of 2025, respectively. The provision in the third quarter of 2026 was primarily driven by decisive action of $17.0 million related to the stressed distillery portfolio and reserves to support continued loan growth


“The fundamental story at Live Oak is that our franchise is getting stronger. Our operating leverage is improving, Live Oak Express continues to accelerate, and our deposit franchise is marching with gaining momentum,” said Live Oak Chairman and CEO James S. (Chip) Mahan III. “The earnings power of this business is expanding because revenue growth is meaningfully outpacing expenses, our loan origination engine is running strong, and our strategic initiatives are delivering results. This operating leverage momentum has aided in absorbing the elevated provision expense in the quarter, which primarily supported record loan growth while also our continued efforts to decisively act to address stress in our distillery-related portfolio. As I think about our operating earnings model, strong loan pipeline, and the possibilities that AI may unlock for both our customers and our employees, I am truly excited about Live Oak’s future.”

The Company considers these adjustments to be relevant to ongoing operating results. The Company believes that excluding the amounts associated with these adjustments to present the non-GAAP financial measures provides a meaningful base for period-to-period comparisons, which will assist regulators, investors, and analysts in analyzing the operating results or financial position of the Company. The non-GAAP financial measures are used by management to assess the performance of the Company’s business for presentations of Company performance to investors, and for other reasons as may be requested by investors and analysts. The Company further believes that presenting the non-GAAP financial measures will permit investors and analysts to assess the performance of the Company on the same basis as that applied by management. Non-GAAP financial measures have inherent limitations, are not required to be uniformly applied, and are not audited. Although non-GAAP financial measures are frequently used by shareholders to evaluate a company, they have limitations as an analytical tool and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for analysis of results reported under GAAP.
